market_holds: Spot about $0.83 (sealed 0.8296 at 18:11 UTC; Yahoo intraday 0.8327 at 19:27 UTC, so the run-day close was not yet final). The stock is down 6.7% today while KWEB was flat and BIDU up 0.3%, down 13.6% over 5 sessions and 12.8% over 20, sits 0.4% above its 52-week low and 63% below its high, and has traded under $1 since mid-October. From the $1.33 close before the Q2 print (Aug 17) to now it is down about 37%. There is no usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided), so no implied move. The real earnings-day reactions, from Yahoo daily bars, were: Q3'25 (Nov 18 2025) +6.3% on a narrower loss; Q4'25 (Feb 26) -3.4% with a further -6% the next day; Q1'26 (May 18) -2.6%; Q2'26 (Aug 18, pre-market release) -7.5%, then about -8% and -9% on the next two days. The median absolute reaction is about 5%. The baseline's own 6-K history mixes in non-earnings dates. Consensus (Earnings Whispers/Finviz preview dated Nov 6-9 2026, Benzinga) is revenue $909M, below Q2's $923.8M and down 2.6% y/y in USD, with EPS -$0.01 against a whisper of +$0.01. The company gives no guidance. Short interest is 70.6m, about 7.3%, 14 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30, per the sweep). T. Rowe Price cut its Class A holding from 17.7% (13G/A, 2026-06-30) to 8.8% (13G/A, event 2026-08-31), so a large holder was exiting during the slide.
view: This looks like a soft quarter going into a stock that has already been marked down for one. The independent content evidence points to a weak summer for iQIYI. In Yunhe Data's Q3 2026 long-drama report (Jul 1-Sep 30), the top three titles by effective views were Youku's 九门 (1.27bn) and 早春晴朗 (1.05bn) and Tencent's 兰香如故. Youku productions filled much of the rest of the leaderboard, and no iQIYI title is named near the top, whereas iQIYI's own heat lists dominated H1. The industry's top-20 dramas were already down 8% y/y in H1. So a sequential membership rebound in Q3, which the preview calls the minimum requirement, looks doubtful, and membership is the line the stock has traded on (Q2: membership -4% q/q, 'seasonality'). Against that, the bar is already low and positioning is bearish. Consensus revenue sits below Q2. The stock has fallen 37% since the last print and 13.6% in the five sessions before this one. Short interest is 14 days to cover. Content-cost cuts gave an 80% q/q narrowing of the non-GAAP operating loss in Q2, so a cost-driven earnings beat with soft revenue is plausible: that is what produced the +6% reaction a year ago. The price trend and the drift after the last three prints lean down. The level of the price and the positioning lean toward a relief bounce on anything less bad. I end slightly below 50 and make no recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The one dated, independent datapoint is iQIYI's absence from the Q3 drama leaderboard, which Youku and Tencent led. It points to soft membership, but consensus revenue is already below Q2 and the stock has fallen 37% since the last print. I cannot show that the weakness is unpriced. Positioning (14 days to cover, 52-week low, sub-$1) makes a relief move on a cost-led beat about as plausible as another leg down.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: If membership revenue rebounds sequentially and the non-GAAP operating result turns positive, the crowded short would likely squeeze the stock up. If membership falls again q/q with a wider loss, the drift after the last three prints would likely repeat downward.

self_critique: The case for up is real. Sentiment and price have already absorbed a bad summer. Consensus models a revenue decline. The short base is large relative to volume. iQIYI's cost discipline and lower amortisation on a thinner slate could produce a profit beat, as the +6% reaction a year ago did. The leaderboard evidence measures effective views, not iQIYI's subscription revenue: its short-drama share (No. 1 in China by June), overseas membership growth of about 40% y/y and content distribution could offset a weak long-drama slate. Against down: Q2 membership already fell 4% q/q and consensus sits below Q2.
approach_notes: P4 (priced-in is a claim to prove) kept me from turning the leaderboard data into a short: the low consensus and the -37% path show at least part of it is priced. P3's freshest-data-first pointed to the Yunhe Q3 report, but its platform split was image-only, so the attribution took several extra searches.
